title: Knowledge check: Component Lifecycle

options: Use lifecycle hooks when the component reaches the required phase, and remove timers, listeners, and subscriptions during cleanup.
Read a DOM element before it has mounted.
Register a global listener on every update without cleanup.
Assume nextTick() runs before Vue’s queued DOM update.
questions.answer_key: Use lifecycle hooks when the component reaches the required phase, and remove timers, listeners, and subscriptions during cleanup.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Component Lifecycle directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “Component creation and setup”, which practice is most reliable?
options: Use a template ref before the element is mounted.
Register duplicate global listeners on every update without cleanup.
nextTick() runs before Vue updates the DOM.
Place DOM-dependent work after mount and clean up listeners or subscriptions when they are no longer needed.
questions.answer_key: Place DOM-dependent work after mount and clean up listeners or subscriptions when they are no longer needed.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “Component creation and setup”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Component Lifecycle” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.
